text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cataplexy secondary to Narcolepsy Type 1 (Suggested by atypical "grimacing/staring" description, short duration, and post-episode confusion/lethargy; however, classic narcolepsy cataplexy presents with sudden muscle weakness. The described "facial grimacing and staring" with a "muddy taste" and post-ictal confusion is highly suggestive of Frontal Lobe Epilepsy with complex partial seizures, possibly originating in the insular or temporal cortex. Further workup needed to confirm seizure semiology vs. rare cataplectic features).

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram), MRI Brain
